text: Ten lessons ago, this whole project started with one sentence from a regional sales manager. Let's recap everything that sentence turned into, and look at where this capstone sequence goes from here.

Lessons one through three turned a vague ask into a written requirement, then a plain-English plan, then a real T-SQL query joining four AdventureWorks2012 tables, filtered to the current quarter, grouped by territory and product line. Lessons four through seven brought that query into Power BI, built three DAX measures, and added a slicer and formatting aimed at a non-technical reader. Lessons eight and nine published the report to the Power BI Service and practiced presenting it, headline first.

None of these lessons were really about SQL or Power BI alone. Lesson one was requirements clarification. Lesson four was data validation — checking a number before trusting it. Lesson nine was clear communication. The tools were the vehicle. Those three skills are what actually made this project succeed, and they transfer to any BI tool you'll ever use.

Just as deliberate as what got built is what got left out. No SSIS, no SSRS, no data warehouse, no year over year trend — because none of that was what the Southeast manager actually asked for. Matching your effort to the real request, and knowing how to scope down, is as real a skill as knowing how to scope up.

You built something real here — a complete, working report, requested, built, published, and presented. The Intermediate project picks up right where this one stopped: more stakeholders, a comparison across time instead of one quarter, and higher stakes. The foundation stays the same. See you there.
